player_0.content: New plan: My previous attempt failed because I underestimated the intensity of "Regretful" and overestimated "Defensive" without fully analyzing the specific emotional arc of the final lines. Richie's accusation ("That's why you left, isn't it?") followed by Jules's confirmation ("I left because you wouldn't listen") directly challenges Richie's self-perception and highlights his failure to communicate, which is a primary driver of regret. While Richie is defensive throughout, the dialogue ends on a note of realization of his own fault rather than just a defensive posture. Next time, I will re-evaluate the final exchange to identify the shift from conflict to realization, assigning a higher score to "Regretful" (likely the dominant emotion) and adjusting "Defensive" downward to reflect that the conversation has moved past pure defense into an acknowledgment of past failures. I will also ensure "Shocked" remains low as the conflict was expected, and "Proud" remains near zero as the dialogue strips away any ego.
